A terminal-native autonomous coding and task agent with persistent memory, agent-created skills, and a messaging gateway that lives on 21+ messaging platforms — 19 native to the gateway plus IRC and Microsoft Teams via plugins (Telegram, Discord, Slack, SMS, Matrix, ...). Runs on local, Docker, SSH, Daytona, Modal, Vercel Sandbox or plugin backends. Works with Nous Portal, OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

Install: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/main/scripts/install.sh | bash` (Linux, macOS, WSL2)

Repo: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent

- [Platform Support](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/getting-started/platform-support): Which operating systems, distribution methods, and features Hermes Agent supports.
- [Android / Termux](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/getting-started/termux): Install Hermes Agent on Android from its signed Termux APT repository

# GBrain Skill Resolver

This is the dispatcher. Skills are the implementation. **Read the skill file before acting.** If two skills could match, read both. They are designed to chain (e.g., ingest then enrich for each entity).

**Routing contract:** each skill's frontmatter `triggers:` array is the
authoritative routing signal — harnesses match inbound messages against it
(see `skills/_AGENT_README.md`). This file is the human-readable dispatch
map of the same routing: one place to scan every skill and its trigger
phrases. If a row here and a skill's frontmatter disagree, the frontmatter
wins; fix the row.

**A gbrain call failed or printed `[AGENT]` or a notice block:** follow the
[agent operator protocol](./conventions/agent-operator-protocol.md). Read the
error's `code` (fall back to `error`), follow `fix.next`, then run `fix.verify`.

## Which gbrain call for which lookup

 
Ask gbrain before you `grep`, `cat`, `ls` or run SQL on the brain checkout: it
reads the index across every source, ranks, filters and names the slug to read
next. With the gbrain MCP server connected, call the tool of the same name
instead of the CLI (one connection, no per-call startup).

| Lookup | CLI | MCP tool |
|---|---|---|
| Find a page by name or path | `gbrain find <name\|prefix\|glob> [--type T] [--source S]` | `find_pages` |
| Count pages by kind or source | `gbrain stats --by source,type [--since 30d] [--collapse-aliases]` | `get_stats` (needs an admin-scope token) |
| Answer a question, search a topic | `gbrain query " " [--types '["meeting"]'] [--since 30d]` | `query` |
| Pages with these words | `gbrain search " " [--match keyword] [--source S]` | `search` |
| Read a known page | `gbrain get ` | `get_page` |
| Read only the part a search hit points at | `gbrain get --around-chunk-id <chunk_id>` or `--lines '{"from":1,"count":200}'` | `get_page` |
| What the brain knows about a person or company | `gbrain entity `, then `gbrain recall " " --json` | `entity`, `recall` |
| Links, dated events, every page of a type | `gbrain backlinks `, `gbrain timeline `, `gbrain list --type T` | `get_backlinks`, `get_timeline`, `list_pages` |
| Save a fact the user stated | `gbrain remember " " --entity --content-origin user_said --provenance " "` | `remember` |
| Why a page didn't rank | `gbrain query " " --explain-target ` | `query` |
| Which installed skill fits a request | `gbrain skills resolve --text " " --json` (after `gbrain skills index build`) | none (CLI only) |
| Find something archived to B2, Supabase or S3 | `gbrain storage-find " "` | `storage_find` |

Parse `--json` output instead of matching the text; notices go to stderr. Never
send stderr to `/dev/null`: a refusal there (`no_brain`, `GBRAIN_DB_ACCESS`)
then reads as "no results"; check the exit code too. Take
`chunk_id` from a fresh `search --json` hit (an old one fails `revision_changed`),
and read a degraded notice before concluding the brain has nothing.

{"output": "Usage: gbrain capture [content] [options]

The single entrypoint for getting content into the brain. One command,
local OR thin-client, synchronous receipt with the resulting page slug.

Modes (mutually exclusive — first match wins):
  gbrain capture "thought"          inline content
  gbrain capture --file PATH        read content from a file
  gbrain capture --stdin            read content from stdin (piped)

Options:
  --slug SLUG          Override the default inbox/YYYY-MM-DD-<hash6> slug
  --type TYPE          Override the page type (default: note)
  --source ID          Multi-source brains: write under a non-default source.
                       Resolution: --source flag > GBRAIN_SOURCE env >
                       .gbrain-source dotfile (walk-up) > local_path >
                       brain_default > 'default'. NOT supported on
                       thin-client installs (server-side OAuth client
                       registration scopes the source).
  --quiet, -q          Print just the slug on stdout (for shell pipelines)
  --json               JSON output for agents
  --request-id UUID     Retry the same logical capture with its original UUID
  --expected-revision UUID  Replace only this version of an existing page
  --force              Explicitly replace an existing page without a revision
  --help, -h           Show this help

Notes:
  - Binary files (image/audio/video/pdf, anything with NUL bytes in the
    first 8KB) are rejected with a friendly error. Use a content-type
    processor skillpack for those when available.
  - Capturing identical text twice produces the same slug and the same
    content_hash (whitespace + line endings + Unicode form are normalized
    before hashing). The daemon's 24h LRU dedup uses this hash.
  - source_kind in the DB is ALWAYS 'capture-cli' for invocations of this
    command. --source maps to the source_id DB column, NOT to source_kind.
    Replacing an existing slug requires --expected-revision or --force.
    Keep --request-id unchanged when retrying the same capture.

Examples:
  gbrain capture "remember to follow up on the X deal"
  echo "from a pipe" | gbrain capture --stdin
  gbrain capture --file ./notes/today.md --slug daily/2026-05-20
  JOB=$(gbrain capture "..." --quiet)

[config] source: file/env plane (~/.gbrain/config.json or env)
gbrain doctor: Check brain health; preview and run remediation.

Usage: gbrain doctor [--fast] [--json] [--fix [--dry-run]] [--scope=brain] [--source <id>] [--no-migrate] [--locks]
       gbrain doctor --tier ops|quick|standard|deep [--budget-ms <n>] [--json]
       gbrain doctor --only <check>[,<check>…] [--tier ops] [--json]
       gbrain doctor --alert [--tier <t>] [--budget-ms <n>] [--json]
       gbrain doctor --remediation-plan [--target-score <n>] [--no-embed] [--json]
       gbrain doctor --remediate [--yes [--expect <plan_hash>]] [--include-repairs] [--max-usd <n>] [--target-score <n>]
                     [--max-jobs <n>] [--no-embed] [--dry-run] [--resume [<plan_hash>]] [--json]

Flags:
  --json                boolean  Print one JSON document (checks, score, findings) on stdout.
  --only <value>        string   Read-only: run just the named checks (comma-separated or repeated; no migrations). The usual fix.verify. An unknown name exits 2 with the valid list.
  --alert               boolean  What an agent cron pages on: runs only the page-class checks (database, writes, migrations, builds, sync and maintenance stalls, corrupt rows, schema exposure, paid-loop breaker), fresh, under a 30 s budget, and exits 0 (alert none), 17 (act: alert.items carry each fix) or 18 (unknown: a page-class check did not run fresh; alert.consecutive_unknown counts the runs in a row). Read-only. With --tier, grades that tier's full run instead.
  --fast                boolean  Skip database checks; filesystem and config checks only.
  --tier <choice>       enum     ops: only the operational sections (capacity, write failures, embedding state, sync movement, compaction, serve build, schema pack) under a 4 s deadline, observational (no migrations). quick: the health gate for agents on large brains: the ops sections plus schema version, sync failures, queue health and partial embeddings under a 10 s deadline; every other check is reported from its last known result with its age, checks with none from the last 24 h are named as unknown, and a background doctor-refresh job is queued to measure them. standard (default): ops first, then the rest; a brain-wide run records each finished check as its last known result. deep: adds full scans (orphan_ratio on brains over 50,000 pages). One of: ops|quick|standard|deep.
  --budget-ms <n>       number   Absolute end-to-end deadline in ms, counted from before the connect (default 4000 with --tier ops; 0: none). A plain non-interactive --json run caps its check run at doctor.default_budget_ms (file plane, default 90000, 0 off) instead. With --only, the named checks get the whole budget. Checks past it report health unknown (reason budget, which budget in details.limit); the report says complete: false.
  --fix                 boolean  Apply the local fixes doctor knows (skill files, stale locks); pair with --dry-run to preview.
  --dry-run             boolean  Preview --fix or --remediate without changing anything.
  --scope <choice>      enum     Pass --scope=brain to skip the skill-file check group (default all). One of: all|brain.
  --source <value>      string   Scope the orphan_ratio check to one source id.
  --skills-dir <value>  string   Override the auto-detected skills/ directory.
  --no-migrate          boolean  Report on the database as-is; do not apply pending schema migrations first.
  --locks               boolean  List idle-in-transaction backends holding locks (Postgres) and exit.
  --probe               boolean  Also send one tiny paid test request to the configured embedding provider (plain doctor never calls a provider). Non-interactive runs need --yes. [consent: paid, egress]
  --probe-pglite        boolean  Run the PGLite runtime probe (a 5-20 s cold start) even when the disk diagnosis explains a failed connect.
  --index-audit         boolean  Report Postgres indexes with zero recorded scans (informational; never drops anything).
  --content-audit       boolean  Scan every page in the content-quality check instead of the first 1000.
  --remediation-plan    boolean  Read-only: the job and repair steps that would raise the brain score, each with its exact command.
  --remediate           boolean  Run the remediation job steps (asks before any work; non-interactive runs need --yes). [consent: paid]
  --yes                 boolean  Authorize the paid job steps (and, with --include-repairs, the repair steps). Capped at the estimate x1.5 without --max-usd. [consent: paid, destructive]
  --expect <value>      string   With --include-repairs: the plan_hash the user approved; a changed plan asks again.
  --include-repairs     boolean  Also run the protected repair steps (local brain host only; needs the user's agreement). [consent: destructive]
  --max-usd <n>         number   Cumulative USD cap across the run and every --resume; authorizes paid steps up to it. [consent: paid]
  --max-cost <n>        number   Alias of --max-usd. [consent: paid]
  --target-score <n>    number   Brain score the job steps aim for (default 90).
  --max-jobs <n>        number   Submit at most this many job steps.
  --no-embed            boolean  Repair steps re-seal or stamp text only (no paid embeddings).
  --resume <value>      string   Resume a budget-stopped --remediate run (optionally naming its plan_hash).

Examples:
  gbrain doctor --json
  gbrain doctor --only harness_wiring --json
  gbrain doctor --remediation-plan --json
  gbrain doctor --remediate --yes --include-repairs --expect <plan_hash> --max-usd 5

A flag marked [consent: …] authorizes that effect: get the user's agreement before passing it.
